title: How Much of an Occupant Supplement Counts as Room Money for Tax, Hotel Rate Plans
content:
Whether the occupant supplement standing on a Hotel Rate Plans folio joins the room money the statutory tax acts on turns on whether such lines are there at all and on whether the rate plan booked includes breakfast.

## The rule

1. Where the folio carries occupant supplement lines and the rate plan booked includes breakfast, 100 percent of the occupant supplement posted is counted as room money.
2. Where the folio carries occupant supplement lines and the rate plan booked does not include breakfast, 0 percent of it is counted as room money.
3. Where the folio carries no occupant supplement line, 0 percent of it is counted as room money.

## Which plans include breakfast

| Rate plan | Breakfast included | Share of the occupant supplement counted, where such lines stand |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Non-Refundable Saver Rate | no | 0 percent |
| Advance Purchase 21 Rate | no | 0 percent |
| Semi-Flexible Rate | no | 0 percent |
| Standard Flexible Rate | yes | 100 percent |
| Member Flex Rate | yes | 100 percent |
| Suite Flexible Rate | yes | 100 percent |
| All-Inclusive Flex Rate | yes | 100 percent |

Where no occupant supplement line stands on the folio, the share is 0 percent on every plan, and 0 percent of nothing is nothing either way.

## Worked on hypothetical figures

An occupant supplement of 240.00 USD standing on the folio:

- On the Suite Flexible Rate, which includes breakfast, 100 percent counts, adding 240.00 USD to the room money.
- On the Semi-Flexible Rate, which does not, 0 percent counts, adding 0.00 USD.
- Where no occupant supplement line stood on the folio at all, 0 percent of nothing would be added on either plan.
